title: Two-step evaluation of a doubled bit
statement: Let $x$ be a binary word, $q$ an evaluation state, $q'$ a verifier control state, $i$ a natural number with $i+2\le |x|$, $u$ a binary word, $h$ an integer, $b$ a bit, and $e$ a head-movement sign. Suppose the bit at index $i$ of $x$ is $b$, and the evaluation action in state $q$ on bit $b$, reading the work-tape cell at $h$ when the tape stores $u$, is the silent move that advances the input head, moves the work head by $e$, and enters $q'$. Then, starting in evaluation state $q$ with $i$ input bits consumed, work word $u$, and work head at $h$, two machine steps reach control state $q'$, with $i+2$ bits consumed, work word $u$, and work head at $h+e$.
hypotheses_covered: $q$ is an evaluation state and $q'$ is a verifier control state
$u$ is a binary word and $h$ is an integer
$b$ is a Boolean bit and $e$ is a head-movement sign
the bit at index $i$ of $x$ is $b$
the evaluation action for $q,b$ and the tape cell at $h$ storing $u$ equals the specified silent move by $e$ into $q'$

integer, and $q$ an evaluation state. Suppose the evaluation action for $q$ on bit $b$,
with the work cell at $h$ of the tape holding $u$, is the silent move advancing the
input head, moving the work head by $e$, and entering $q'$. Then from the
non-tautology verifier's evaluation configuration carrying $q$ with $i$ bits consumed,
work word $u$, and head $h$, two steps reach state $q'$ with $i+2$ bits consumed and
head $h + e$.
